text:
Barker 实操：2 万 U 自己跑资费套利年化 12%，真的不用盯盘吗？-----量化白捡篇

我们自己拿真钱在 Hyperliquid 上跑了 76 天，折算年化 12.33%。期间 HYPE 涨了快一倍，账户始终对冲着。钱包地址公开，每一笔链上可查。

策略代码现在全部开源！！！也准备了 Claude 自动跑方案一键执行，参数看的头疼也不用懂，交给 AI，放在了文末免费取用！

策略很简单，买一份 HYPE 现货，同时开等量的 HYPE 空单。

币涨，现货赚、空单亏；币跌，反过来。数量一样，涨跌抵消。你不管方向，只收空单那边每小时的资金费。

【76 天的账，拆开看】

｜收到的资金费：+880 USDC（1,822 次结算）
｜付出的资金费：-61（费率为负的小时）
｜借款利息：-184（平均年利率约 5.1%）
｜交易手续费：-50（317 笔成交）
｜两腿价差：+5
｜净收益：约 +589 USDC

赚的几乎全是资金费，最大的开销是借 USDC 的利息。手续费主要花在建仓和退出，两边都吃单的话开平一轮约为仓位的 0.23%，拿得越久越不值一提。

【先定仓位：借不借钱，借多少】

统一保证金让你可以借 USDC 把仓位做大。按这 76 天的平均资金费和借款利率算，未扣手续费：

｜本金的 0.8 倍，不借钱：年化约 8.1%
｜1.0 倍，借 0.1 倍：约 9.6%
｜1.4 倍，借 0.54 倍：约 11.5%
｜1.75 倍，借 0.93 倍：约 13.1%

借得越多收得越多，但大涨时要更早减仓。第一次做，1.3～1.5 倍之间够了，我们实盘平均 1.46 倍。

【怎么做，六步】

门槛：Hyperliquid 账户 1 万美元以上，开通前账户里不能有持仓。以 2 万 USDC、1.5 倍为例：

1. 存 USDC 进去，账户模式切到 Portfolio Margin（统一保证金）
2. 算仓位：单边 3 万 USDC 的 HYPE，系统会自动借约 1.3 万 USDC
3. 分 5 批买：现货页挂限价单买入，成交后马上去永续页开同样数量的空单
4. 核对：现货和空单数量一样，账户风险指标 PMR 在 0.65 以下，能看到借款金额和利率。也可以去 Hyperliquid Eco 网站输自己地址，Positions 看空单、Lending 看现货和借款
5. 放着。资金费每小时自动到账，利息自动扣
6. 想退出：分批卖现货，同时平掉同样数量的空单，借的钱自动还上。确认借款归零、没有残余仓位，再提回钱包

【什么时候要动手】

平时每天看一眼这四个数：

｜PMR：0.65 以下正常，超过 0.8 就减仓，0.95 被清算
｜借款健康度（Lending 一栏的 Health Factor）：1.3 以上正常，低于 1 不能再自动借，空单亏了要自己补 USDC
｜现货和空单数量：差得明显就补齐
｜资金费收入 vs 借款利息：长期盖不住就考虑退

要动手的主要是一种情况：币大涨。1.5 倍仓位下，HYPE 涨约 83% PMR 到 0.8，涨约 210% 到清算线。所以到 0.8 就减一点，别等。

我们这 76 天经历过一次：HYPE 从 55 美元涨到 98 美元，减过一次仓，PMR 最高到 0.62，没碰过线。

【什么时候会亏】
资金费变负：看跌的人多了，换你付钱。这 76 天约 9.5% 的小时是负的，最长连续 8 小时；历史最差的一周按年化约 -11.9%。

借款利息涨：资金池利用率超过 80% 后利率涨得很快，盖过资金费就是亏。

现货和永续短时脱节：9 月 17 日 HYPE 现货两分钟内跌了 7%，永续没动，12 分钟后恢复。我们的仓位扛过去了，但偏离持续更久是会亏的。

极端行情：平台可能强制平掉你的空单，现货就裸着了，要赶紧平现货或重新开空。

【不想手动，让 AI 帮你跑】

我们实盘用的代码已开源，自动配对建仓、控两腿价差、监控风险。仓库里带了 AI skill，用 Claude Code 或 Codex 打开就能配置和部署，改参数直接说人话：「仓位小一点」「资金费连续一天为负就提醒我」。先让它把每一步讲明白，再上。

完整文章、每张图、开源仓库地址都在这👇

后续会出更多小白也能上手的简单策略

text:
就在今天，Anthropic 在旧金山总部开了一场不对外的会。邀请的都是投资人

我把这些信息碎片拼到了一起，带你一起过一遍这个会议，以及你需要知道的所有数字

看完之后你会心里有数，AI 的钱，是不是要花不动了？这阵子网上很多人这么说。芯片股连着跌，也有人开始唱衰 Anthropic。

1/ 今年三个季度的收入
一季度 47 亿美元
二季度 116 亿美元
三季度 168 亿美元

2/ 去年一整年，Anthropic 的收入不到 46 亿美元 
今年光一季度，就超过了去年全年。
前三季度加起来 331 亿，是去年全年的 7 倍多

3/ 最近的三个月，超过前六个月。
上半年合计 163 亿，三季度一个季度就是 168 亿

4/ 三季度平均每天收入 1.83 亿美元，每小时 760 万。
就这个吸金能力，你想想看

5/ 去年按经营口径，它亏了 80 多亿美元
今年三季度，公司告诉投资人，按调整后口径已经盈利，现金流为正 

6/ 这场会是给 IPO 铺路的。路透说目标估值 2 万亿美元以上，上市大概率推到 11 月中期选举之后 

但是，我想浇个冷水

增速确实在降。二季度环比涨了 147%，三季度是 45%，单季新增从 69 亿降到 52 亿。放缓，这的确没错

回到开头那个问题。AI 的钱能不能一直这么花下去，最后要看模型公司能不能从客户手里收到钱。Anthropic 今天给的答案是一个季度 168 亿，而且还在涨。它还承诺，未来十年在云服务、算力和基础设施上至少花 5180 亿美元 

看完这组数，我觉得市场太拧巴了：一边是市场担心算力发展减缓，给半导体股票压价；一边是 AI 基建、大模型公司在疯狂扩张

我该信谁的？

text:
卧槽！Claude 的手感为什么这么舒服，这下终于被我扒明白了😁😁😁

Claude 的丝滑并不只是调色好看
有非常多埋在底层的一套工程交互物理学和手感调优细节
对我们 vibecoding 也很有参考价值

前两条帖子好多人在评论区蹲，这次直接交作业
用 REA @morluto  把 Claude Desktop 逆了一遍
整理成一份 3000 多行的逆向手册，附带具体的算法实现，全部开源，欢迎体验，也欢迎提出意见👇

👉 https://t.co/lGIJpv0Wto

建议把仓库发给你的 Agent，让他根据你的项目给出优化方案👍

手册拆成了 7 章，具体的算法拆解和还原细节可以看仓库里的文档
还有 30 个能直接复制的 React 组件

大逆向时代彻底到来，这下真的人人都是 Claude 设计总监了🤣😭😭

1️⃣ 滚动边缘不是一刀切掉
普通线性 Gradient 在高分屏上有明显的切断感。Claude 手写了七档精调的非线性透明阶梯，搭配触顶触底动态归零传感器，呈现出一种水雾般的平滑渐隐效果。

2️⃣ 语音波形加入了 8% 的噪声降噪，语音波形只跟着人声跳，低于 8% 的环境声底噪直接切掉，再做一次 0.7 次方压缩，小声说话被放大，大声也不会炸

3️⃣ 拒绝千篇一律的 ease-out 动效，官方在给按钮、消息卡片、勾选、吸附等分别实现了特调的弹簧参数与手感调优
按钮轻弹一下，0.22 秒归位，卡片展开 0.35 秒停住，勾选成功会跳两下，拖侧边栏零回弹，松手就像被磁铁吸住

4️⃣ AI 吐字时屏幕自动跟着滚
但你只要往上一滑，150 毫秒内立刻松手，绝不把你拽回底部

5️⃣ 看图放大以鼠标为中心，不是傻傻地从屏幕中间放大
移动不到 4px 不算拖，手抖也不怕

6️⃣ 拖分栏划过网页预览也不会卡死，双击一下直接五五对半

接下来是不是可以继续分析一下 Claude 的 Web 端 🤣🤣🤣

专业的事还得专业的人来做，这下真快把 Claude 的前端全蒸馏完了：

REA 挖出来的 Claude 细节，好多技术名词我见都没见过

比如 AI 往外吐字的时候，屏幕会自动跟着往下滚
界面几乎不用黑色边框，靠 4 层深浅差一点点的底色分出层次

黑夜模式下，按钮和卡片不用外面那圈白边
是在里面贴一道很淡的亮线来达到同样的视觉效果
在 Mac 的高清屏上，分割线会自动变细到 0.5px

text:
Now that AI agents can own an outcome from start to finish, how do you sell them?

1. Sell the platform:

License the agent to a company to run in its own operations. No existing contract sets the price, so there's more upside, but new budgets take time to approve and results are harder to credit to the agent.

2. Sell the service:

Take over work a company already outsources, the way Red Ventures sold policies for insurers and got paid per policy closed. The budget already exists, so deals close faster, but the highest-value work usually runs in-house, which caps the upside.

3. Go full-stack:

Become the business, like buying debt portfolios and collecting on them yourself. You keep all the value the AI creates, but you also take on the licensing and compliance.

Full piece from a16z's @dhaber on long-running agents in high-value customer journeys: https://t.co/aHaatcizcd

text:
新疆淡水资源非常丰富，很多优质湖适合高品质养鱼，但是鲜鱼运不出去，成本没有优势，只能养虹鳟这种高密度高价值刺身鱼，

本来当地养得好好的，结果一群人张牙舞爪说抵制日本常用的大西洋鲑，跑到国家食品监管机构顺势把淡水虹鳟纳入三文鱼标准，

结果不仅毁了整个三文鱼产业，也毁了新疆虹鳟产业， 在整个中国把“三文鱼”这三个字搞信用破产了，

老百姓只认准“大西洋鲑”，商家只给你标注“大西洋鲑”，任何“三文鱼”不止代表你用了新疆虹鳟，而且代表你骗了我，你是个大骗子，“三文鱼=新疆虹鳟=以次充好=你在骗我”。

后来撒贝宁开车去赛里木湖录节目，说赛里木湖太美了，人这辈子一定要去一趟赛里木湖。

本来也挺好的，都知道新疆西边和南边有一大片树林草原大湖泊，景色不错，还没什么人，一群人自己掏钱去消费拉动经济，

结果一车人为了停车费被当地人抱团直接打了一顿，后续直接罚款+辞职+行政拘留就完事儿了，从此没人敢去赛里木湖。

你拉动GDP是好事，带动就业是好事，在当地投资扶贫也是好事儿，

但是你每次都这么玩儿，新疆本地也压根不管，以后谁他妈还敢去，别人谁爱吃虹鳟吃虹鳟，谁爱旅游谁旅游去吧。

很多人喊口号不长记性，听口号也不长记性，必须让事情教你一遍，你才长记性。

text:
Theophyseval固然是一个很大的进展，但物理和数学两个学科的构造范式的差异决定了ai在两个领域的突破速度存在本质差异。

数学是一场在形式系统内部展开的逻辑远征。它立足于一组无矛盾的自洽公理（如欧几里得几何或 ZFC 公理系统），沿着形式逻辑规则向外推导定理。对数学而言，“真理”是公理网络内部的演绎闭包，它具备永恒性与无尺度特性（Scale-Free）——费马大定理在普朗克尺度成立，在星系尺度成立，在任何维度的虚构宇宙中同样成立。它追求的是独立于经验观察之外的必然性。

物理学则相反，它是一门关于信息压缩与尺度解耦（Decoupling of Scales）的艺术。物理世界的精妙之处在于：微观底层的极端复杂性，会在宏观尺度上被自动平均。如果研究流体力学必须从夸克和胶子的强相互作用算起，人类的认知与计算早在数个世纪前便已瘫痪。

因此，现代物理学的核心哲学不是追求形式上的“绝对穷尽”，而是有效场论（Effective Field Theory）与粗粒化（Coarse-Graining）。通过对无关高频自由度的主动丢弃，物理学家提炼出系统在特定能量截断（Cutoff）或空间尺度下的关键自由度，用最具对称性与最小作用量的精炼方程去预测现实。物理理论从来不是全知全能的绝对真理，而是在特定窗口内以最小信息成本逼近现实的最优投影。

这种方法论的分野，直接构成了ai在两门学科中扩张阻力（Scaling Friction）的物理屏障。

AI 能够在象棋、围棋乃至形式数学中迅速逼近乃至超越顶尖人类，核心前提在于它拥有一个确定性的形式验证器（Self-contained Verifier）。在 Lean、Isabelle 等形式化语言环境中，命题的真伪检验纯粹是符号匹配与逻辑遍历。AI 可以在数字空间内自行生成猜想、自我博弈并执行无止境的强化学习（RL Self-Play）。其试错成本仅是算力与电费，边际延迟趋近于零。

物理学却缺乏数字闭环。物理理论的最终判决者不是逻辑自洽性，而是真实的物理世界。它的外部验证器是大型强子对撞机（LHC）、韦伯太空望远镜、托卡马克装置或高能激光系统。即便 AI 在数字空间内构想出某种精巧自洽的统一场论，只要它未能经过经验观测的证伪检验，它就不是物理学。现实世界的物理实验受制于工程周期、高昂预算以及仪器信噪比，这种极端狭窄的数据接口，切断了 AI 在纯虚拟环境中自我闭环进化的可能。

在形式系统中，AI 依靠超大状态空间中的非线性搜索击败人类；但在物理学中，最核心的智力挑战从来不是“解方程”，而是“决定忽略什么”。

从含有 10的23次方 个微观粒子的多体系统中抽象出朗道费米液体理论，依赖的是对能量尺度、对称性破缺与重整化群流向的主动剪裁。
纯粹的数据驱动模型天然倾向于在大自由度数据中拟合统计相关，极易引入多余的高阶微观耦合；让神经网络发现规律相对容易，但让它自发领悟哪些相互作用项是应当舍弃的“无关算符”，并写出一个只有三项主导项的精炼拉格朗日量，依然面临严峻的归纳偏置限制。

此外，依靠现有物理规律生成合成数据，充其量只能让 AI 成为偏微分方程的高效数值加速器；而物理学的范式革命（如相对论或量子力学）必须从偏离既有理论的反常实验数据（Anomalies）中诞生。
这种极其稀缺的经验反常，无法在 GPU 集群内部靠自言自语无中生有。

数学提供了一座规则明确、内部自足的逻辑晶体，AI 能够在其中化身为自主的“证明者”；物理学则扎根于尺度分层、充满噪声的物质宇宙，它要求认知主体在有限能标下进行审慎的信息丢弃与仪器对话。

在机器能够自主操控精密物理仪器、闭环设计真实实验并学会对自由度进行审美裁剪之前，人类在物理学前沿的地位依然稳固。人类受限于算力，但 AI 目前受限于尺度直觉与物理世界的真实接口。

以 Codex 框架接入的GPT-6-Astra达到了 98% 的最终答案准确率，而且还是以极低的计算成本，单题求解平均成本 低于 3 美元。

text:
Introducing Procedures.

Agents are probabilistic. Each time they run, they decide again where to pull the data and how to calculate the answer. Two runs of the same question can return two different numbers.

A procedure makes that path deterministic. It takes a run you've validated and turns its steps into code. The steps are fixed, so every run returns the same number.

Finance needs both. Deterministic work is best for the numbers themselves, and probabilistic work is best for the analysis and explanation behind them.

Procedures are now live in @Concourse_ai.

text:
现在很多 Agent 自进化，大致走两条路：

一条改模型权重，一条改 Harness。

这篇 Evo² 直接把两条路接了起来。

系统里，同一个模型同时扮演两个角色：

Proposer 负责修改 Harness，Reflector 负责看执行结果、分析哪里改对了、哪里还需要修。

关键在下一步。

这些 Harness 修改和真实执行结果，会继续拿回来训练 Proposer 和 Reflector。模型变得更会改 Harness，新的 Harness 又产生更好的训练经验，形成一个持续循环。

结果是 Evo² 在 Polyglot 上达到 82.1%，最强 baseline 是 62.6%；SWE-bench Verified 达到 48.3%，相比 baseline 的 41.0% 继续提升。

而且进化出来的 Harness 可以直接迁移到其他 benchmark，不需要重新搜索。固定 GPT-5-mini 权重时，仅靠这套 Harness 进化流程，也把表现从 24.4% 提升到 48.3%。

这篇真正往前推的一步，是让「改进者」本身也进入了学习循环。

以后自进化 Agent 可能会越来越像两个互相促进的系统：

一边积累更好的外部运行结构，一边训练出更会修改这些结构的模型。

当「怎么让自己变强」也开始被持续训练，self-evolution 才真正有了第二层递归。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/pfHcHHL7BF

而且进化出来的 Harness 可以直接迁移到其他 benchmark，不需要重新搜索。固定 GPT-5-mini 权重时，仅靠这套 Harness 进化流程，也把表现从 24.4% 提升到 48.3%。

这篇真正往前推的一步，是让「改进者」本身也进入了学习循环。

以后自进化 Agent 可能会越来越像两个互相促进的系统：

一边积累更好的外部运行结构，一边训练出更会修改这些结构的模型。

当「怎么让自己变强」也开始被持续训练，self-evolution 才真正有了第二层递归。

this trading prompt is f*cking gold

stop asking AI to "build a profitable strategy."

make it explain exactly when to enter, when to exit, and when the entire idea is wrong.

i wrote one prompt that turns "buy the dip" into a mean reversion strategy specification:

reference price → deviation → entry → sizing → exit → invalidation

then it has to walk through three scenarios:

a winning trade.
a losing trade.
a setup it should refuse to trade.

no code until the rules are explicit.
no invented backtest results.
no hiding behind "price should bounce."

the full prompt is in the image.

save it before your next strategy build.

我做 OPC（一人公司）14 个月，定价从一个月 2000 块涨到 7000 块，同时陪跑 8-15 家 AI 公司。中间最难的不是找客户——口碑起来之后客户基本都是老带新。最难的是最开始那一步：搞清楚自己离了原来的公司，到底还能卖什么。

40 多场用户访谈下来，我发现想做 OPC 的人几乎都卡在同一个地方。有能力，但说不清楚能交付什么；知道自己值钱，但不知道怎么定价；接了第一单，不知道怎么验收怎么收尾。

我把这条路上反复出现的卡点——从找方向、服务产品化、验证需求、定价到交付复盘——做成了一个 OPC AI 教练 Skill。它不会给你一套模板让你填空，而是根据你当前卡在哪一步，每次问一个具体的问题，推你做一个 15 分钟能完成的小动作，拿到真实反馈再决定下一步。

text:
一年前，我在 Berkeley AI 投资峰会主持 AI for Healthcare panel，开场问的是：AI 能被信任吗？

一年后，硅谷101 峰会的 AI for Science panel 上，这个问题没人再问了。

大家问的是：AI 的发现，验证得过来吗？瓶颈搬家了 👇
- 2025：卡在医院。工作流、责任、信任，一个系统里跑着 100 个模型，彼此还会互相干扰。
- 2026：卡在湿实验。细胞实验几天，小鼠一个月，临床好几年。

一年里变得最快的三件事：
- 虚拟患者还停在演讲里，虚拟细胞已经拿到 18 亿美元投资
- 药企从只出钱，变成主动交数据
- agent 从跑流程，变成自己去做发现

@luzhangvc 老师两年都在。主线一年没变：数据孤岛、垂直小模型、临床试验。
变的是证据：从"一家做细胞治疗的公司"，变成了拿下诺和诺德项目的 Cellular Intelligence。

判断没变，证据越来越硬。这个赛道开始兑现了。

text:
after switching our approach to building a "FirmOS", I'm increasingly confident that the future of agent collaboration within organizational settings is going to be a "company operating system" or CompanyOS, designed for agent and human collaboration

instead of a "company brain" that holds everything, the OS is for storing rules, processes, decisions made, which tools to use and how. it can mirror some data, but the source of truth is often best held in your existing tools (CRM, etc.). it's continuously updated and used by your agents

i think of this as a "flipped playbook" where instead of writing down the company rules first and following them (which is kind of like waterfall development), you're constantly updating the playbook as you decide or learn new things day-to-day running the business

AI 编程党注意了！TypeScript 大佬 Matt Pocock 列了你可能正在犯的 18 个错，1 张图带你速通！🫣

比如这几条：
1️⃣ 推理强度开得太高
2️⃣ Skill 写得太长
3️⃣ 盯 Agent 盯得太紧
4️⃣ Agent 干完活，没法自己验证对不对
5️⃣ 全局规则文件塞得太满

不过有网友吐槽好几条互相打架，比如「开工前没对齐」和「对齐得太勤太狠」。Matt 说要看任务，小改动先让 AI 改完，再回头对齐。

建议可以把这张图丢给你的 Agent，让它结合你的项目逐条查一遍~

1个人，16天，Opus5.5，200w-300w，干爆一个48G电脑的显存，我真的再次觉得AI让一切都有可能，虽然我们早已知道，Opus4.5的时候，就已经能够做出还比较优质的场景、动画、游戏等等了，但不够具象化

但今天我们应该看到了这是我见过AI快速完成做的最好的游戏，这是Opus5.5在游戏领域的最佳实践了！！！

我做梦都想做一些好玩的游戏，前几天还在跟一些朋友聊天，说觉得现在有了AI完全不需要上班了，AI已经能够带来ROI百倍的效益，甚至公司的运转已经可以让AI来完成大部分了，这句话放在现在中国的任何一家公司，都会受到极大的争议，但sac佬真的能让这件事儿成真，如果上架到Steam，不考虑法律风险的话，这个东西绝对是会卖爆的

SAC佬是真的牛逼，他做的很好的一点，我觉得他就是把工具之间的串联做的特别好，并且给对应的工具做了特别好的分工，这件事如果是我来做的话，我可能是会一个下述的流程去做，等有时间了，我也要玩，做一个玩！

1、Claude Opus 5.5：核心编码、场景逻辑、流程编排、甚至部分设计文档和宣传视频方向的生成
2、Tripo AI：快速生成3D模型（角色、星球元素、道具）

- Alexandr Wang, Meta Chief AI Officer, in an interview with David Senra published October 11.

I love thinking of AutoResearch as Idea Descent: a metric of interest goes down, as a function of ideas/experiments, where the agents get pulled towards one idea or another. But we've seen very often an agent develop this weird tunnel vision, and honing in just one type of "idea", kinda like GD stuck in a local minimum. 

We studied this and seems we can fix it with Fork-and-Flush, a super simple and kinda cute idea. Every so often, fork the agent into T copies in the same workspace but empty the context, let them run for a bit, and continue from the best one. 

If you like the GD analogy, it's basically basin hopping https://t.co/NOzpRGT3It.

BTW we found a silly way of also plotting "idea basins": an LLM rewrites every experiment as a spec and answers a few thousand binary queries "is Experiment A closer to B or to C?". Then we embed this NXN matrix into 2D and indeed see in many cases that each run saturates into a small region and keeps polishing it. 

We call these idea basins!

At equal compute Fork and Flush beats single runs and best-of-N on 12/13 long-horizon tasks (some 4+ days), and in my own research projects it's been working really well! 

BTW we only use it at test time, but it could also be part of training or RL. 

Led by @jackcai1206  @christos_ziakas  during Jack's internships with us, along with @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 @Tea_Pearce Sid Sen and Akshay Krishnamurthy.

CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen in his post-match banquet speech: 

"We had imagined the night to go differently. The first half was a half that we wish it would had gone differently. We made mistakes that we don't want to see. So we have to say that Viking deservedly took the lead. We could see why they won their last 10 games in this stadium and won the league last season. The second half was different. The team showed energy and showed their real level. We turned things around in 17 minutes. In the stands we thought to ourselves: 'yes, this game is now ours, we're winning this' - but then unfortunately we made unnecessary mistakes and got a red card. In the end, a 3-3 draw was probably a fair outcome. Now we have 7 games in the next 22 days. We have to look ahead despite the disappointment of today"

text:
种种迹象表明，一场30年来规模最大的债务大清洗正在中国悄然上演

很多人还在盯着房价涨跌，却没注意到一场足以改写普通人命运的财富洗牌已经悄悄开始了。

2024年底，国家一口气推出12万亿化债组合拳，计划在2028年之前，把地方政府的隐性债务从14.3万亿压缩至2.3万亿。

12万亿什么概念？
相当于全国人一整年可支配收入的四分之一。

你以为这只是政府自己还债的事，跟你没半点关系？错了。历史已经两次证明，每一次大规模化债都伴随着一场财富的重新洗牌。

1999年化债之后，打开了商品房时代，有人拿着下岗补偿买了房，20年后资产翻了几十倍。2015年化债之后，打开了棚改货币化，有人冲进三四线楼市，赚得盆满钵满。这一次，12万亿化债组合拳已经启动，新的蓄水池正在打开。谁先看懂钱往哪流，谁就能先喝到水。

先说第一次，发生在上世纪90年代末，那时候四大国有银行坏账成山，坏账率高达30%左右，按国际标准早就该破产了。什么概念？银行每放出去100块钱的贷款，有30块可能收不回来，整个金融系统随时可能崩盘。

国家怎么化债？
1999年一口气成立了四家资产管理公司，从四大行手里按原价接走了1.4万亿的坏账，财政部掏了400亿注册资本，央行提供了5700亿再贷款，四大行发了8200亿金融债券，硬是把这笔天文数字的烂账给剥离了。四大行甩掉了包袱，轻装上阵，后来纷纷上市，变成了全世界最赚钱的银行。但关键不在化债本身，而在于国家同步打开了什么蓄水池。就在1998年，福利分房取消了，商品房时代正式开启。那时候，北京的房价才一千多块一平米。很多刚下岗的工人，口袋里揣着几万块买断工龄的钱。站在人生的十字路口，有人咬牙买了房，有人觉得房子不靠谱，把钱存进了银行。

二十多年后回头看，买了房的那批人，资产翻了几十倍，不少人就此完成了阶层跨越，这不是运气，是因为他们踩在了那个时代最大的蓄水池上。

第二次化债发生在2015年，根源还是2008年。4万亿刺激之后，大量钱通过地方融资平台涌进基建。路修了，桥建了，债也欠了一屁股。到了2014年，地方政府存量债务达到15.4万亿，其中超过九成是银行贷款、信托。

这些非债券方式的借款平均利率在10%左右，光还利息就喘不过气来。怎么化债？
从2015年开始，国家用了四年时间发行了12.2万亿地方置换债券，把高息的短期债务全部换成低息的长期债券，以时间换空间，把地方政府从还债的泥潭里拽了出来。

这次的蓄水池是什么？
棚改货币化，央行通过PSL把钱注入政策性银行，政策性银行再贷给地方政府，搞棚改拆迁，拆迁户拿着现金冲进楼市。

几年时间棚改向市场投放了数万亿资金，结果大家都看到了，三四线城市的房价被硬生生推了起来，很多原本没人问津的城市房价翻了一倍甚至更多。资本市场也在那两年经历了一轮行情，你看规律出来了，1999年化债蓄水池是一线城市的楼市，2015年化债蓄水池是三四线楼市加资本市场。两次的载体不同，但逻辑完全一样。

化债本身会释放巨大的流动性，这些钱必须有地方去，国家会引导它们留下某个出口，而那个出口就是财富机会的入口。

那这一次的蓄水池是什么？
这一次的规模更大，动作也更系统。

12万亿化债组合拳落地之后，短短一年多，地方隐性债务就从14.3万亿降到了10.5万亿，一年少了将近4万亿，债务平均利息成本降低超过2.5个百分点，五年累计能省下利息超过4500亿。更关键的是，全国超过六成的融资平台已经退出，今年又有34个城市宣布隐性债务清零。

这些数字说明什么？
政府正在大规模地卸下包袱，腾出来的钱和精力要投向新的方向。这些省下来的钱去哪了？配套推进的是国有资产证券化、基础设施、REITs、科技创新债等一系列新方向。

大量原本躺在地方政府账本上的公路、能源、数据等基础设施，开始被包装成可以交易的金融产品推向市场。湖北、安徽已经率先喊出了三化战略，资产化、证券化、杠杆化，说白了就是把沉睡的国有资产变成真金白银。这和当年楼市一样，是在为超发的流动性打开一个新出口。

有人会问，这次不同以往，会不会只是昙花一现？
这个疑问可以理解，但你想想，1999年很多人也不信房子能涨，觉得住单位分的房就够了，2015年也有一大批人觉得三四线楼市没戏，犹豫着没下手。结果呢？

每一次大规模化债，都不是一两年的短期刺激，而是一个持续5到10年的结构性变化。债务置换要好几年才能完成，配套改革也不是一蹴而就的，每一步都在不断释放新的政策信号和资金流向。

还有个关键点很少人注意到，2026年是6万亿置换债收官之年，这标志着化债工作从债务置换转向构建长效机制。财政部刚成立了债务管理司，专门盯全口径债务风险防控。城投公司要在2027年6月前全部完成退出，从准政府债变成真正的市场化信用主体。

这意味着什么？
整个地方政府的融资逻辑在彻底重建，旧模式结束了，新模式正在建立，房地产这个旧蓄水池装不下了，新蓄水池正在成型。这个过程会持续很多年，期间会有大量的交易机会和财富重新分配。

还有个关键点很少人注意到，2026年是6万亿置换债收官之年，这标志着化债工作从债务置换转向构建长效机制。财政部刚成立了债务管理司，专门盯全口径债务风险防控。城投公司要在2027年6月前全部完成退出，从准政府债变成真正的市场化信用主体。

这意味着什么？
整个地方政府的融资逻辑在彻底重建，旧模式结束了，新模式正在建立，房地产这个旧蓄水池装不下了，新蓄水池正在成型。这个过程会持续很多年，期间会有大量的交易机会和财富重新分配。

现在出版一本书，已经非常容易了

刚才在联邦政府网站 https://t.co/5oPx55Q8LO 上，申请了一个“国际标准书号”（ISBN，见图）。

无论是加拿大公司，还是个人自出版作者，都可以免费申请。

到时候，把书稿和封面上传给 Draft2Digital（简称 D2D），就可以通过它在十多家平台上架，面向世界各地的读者。

格式转换、发行和版税结算，都可以交给它处理，等于有了一个出版发行代理。

电子书方面，D2D 的佣金约为零售价的10%，书店通常另外抽取约30%，作者大约拿到60%。

这是非独家发行，作者仍然可以通过其他渠道卖书。

它也提供纸质书的按需印刷，作者可以按作者自购价订购一些，支付印刷、运费等费用，拿回来送人或自行销售。

以前复杂又昂贵的出版，如今已经变得这么容易了。

text:
A new paper from Apple engineers ends with a line we couldn’t have written better ourselves:

"if idle macOS devices across organizations [...] can be securely federated, they could form a massive, shared GPU resource pool that benefits the broader ecosystem."

That’s what we’re building with Darkbloom.

The paper's Minions is a system that pool idle Apple Silicon Macs into a distributed GPU cloud for on-prem inference. Queue times went from 10+ hours to minutes. Zero new GPU purchases. Zero infrastructure cost.

It runs inside Apple, on coworkers’ Macs, using the company’s own storage and access controls. When a team needs more capacity, they Slack colleagues and ask them to turn on the executor. Even in that setting, the top adoption concern was data confidentiality. People were wary of their jobs running on a colleague’s Mac. Apple’s fix was to keep each team’s work on its own team’s machines.

Which brings it back to that one word in the conclusion: “securely.”

Inside a company, you can shrink the network until you trust everyone in it. On an open network, the machine belongs to a stranger and there’s no one to Slack. Keeping prompts private and outputs honest on hardware you don’t control is the hard problem that we solved at Darkbloom.

Apple built the on-prem version. 
Darkbloom is the open one.

result.text:
A new paper from Apple engineers ends with a line we couldn’t have written better ourselves:

"if idle macOS devices across organizations [...] can be securely federated, they could form a massive, shared GPU resource pool that benefits the broader ecosystem."

That’s what we’re building with Darkbloom.

The paper's Minions is a system that pool idle Apple Silicon Macs into a distributed GPU cloud for on-prem inference. Queue times went from 10+ hours to minutes. Zero new GPU purchases. Zero infrastructure cost.

It runs inside Apple, on coworkers’ Macs, using the company’s own storage and access controls. When a team needs more capacity, they Slack colleagues and ask them to turn on the executor. Even in that setting, the top adoption concern was data confidentiality. People were wary of their jobs running on a colleague’s Mac. Apple’s fix was to keep each team’s work on its own team’s machines.

Which brings it back to that one word in the conclusion: “securely.”

Inside a company, you can shrink the network until you trust everyone in it. On an open network, the machine belongs to a stranger and there’s no one to Slack. Keeping prompts private and outputs honest on hardware you don’t control is the hard problem that we solved at Darkbloom.

Apple built the on-prem version. 
Darkbloom is the open one.

text:
一些已经财务自由的朋友问，不要工资，有没有门路去 frontier lab 工作。这些 frontier lab 的回答是，每个人消耗的 GPU 成本和 token 成本远超他们的工资，一个不能胜任的人浪费的资源不是不要工资就能弥补的。

DeepSeek 刘胜宇把今年夏天以来的算子开发比作 “机甲驾驶员”。LLM 正在逐渐制造业化，机器的成本超过人的成本（虽然人仍然很贵），工程经验比 raw intelligence 更重要，social closure 正在形成。

创业以来接触了很多财务自由的人，财务自由只能给你拒绝工作的自由、消费的自由，不能给你创造的自由。

很多财务自由的人甚至连拒绝工作的自由都没有，比如很多上市公司高管，公司就像自己的孩子，必须一直负责下去，没有心思赶新的技术浪潮。

要获得创造的自由，也就是自由进入自己想做的领域，我只想到三条路：
1. 自己深入学习另一个领域，转行，比如从天坑专业转码；AI 可以让我们更快地入门和探索新领域，但要达到顶尖水平，仍然很难，因为专业圈子都像 LLM 这样存在 social closure。
2. 在一个领域取得成果、声誉和影响力，从而可以通过项目合作、顾问等方式进入感兴趣的其他领域，甚至横跨多个领域；（可以是公司内，比如做网络的专家也需要参与芯片、OS 等部门的讨论和合作；也可以是跨公司的）
3. 具备讲故事、拉团队、整合资源的能力，比如很多优秀创始人并非技术背景。

quotedTweet.text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
兄弟们，看了一圈  Gemini 4 Argon 在2D转3D方面确实遥遥领先。别再以为搞 3D 必须开 Blender 熬夜雕面调骨骼了。
看看原推这玩意儿，直接把我给看清醒了：
给模型一张 2D 维多利亚马车图，零人工参与，纯靠代码直接吐出了一个完整的 WebGL 交互级 3D 资产！扒了一下原推的关键实测数据，极其哈人：

1. 纯代码暴力建构：整整 17.4 万面（Face），没动哪怕一秒 Blender，全是程序化几何直接生成；
2. 带复杂物理装配：不是死模型！车门能开合、车窗带铰链、车轮自带真实的悬挂与回弹物理；
3. 高阶细节与着色：车头的提灯自带动态烛光闪烁，甚至车身上还雕刻了完整的立体骷髅浮雕。大部分人以为大模型只会写两行前端页面或者生成 2D 废话。

真正的技术降维是：大模型正在把图形学渲染管线和几何拓扑当成底层指令直接编译。独立开发者以后做 3D 网页展厅、轻量小游戏，生产力直接被暴力拉平几百倍。
懂 Three.js 和 WebGL 渲染管线的兄弟帮掌掌眼，这种代码生成的拓扑放移动端能扛住几帧？👇 https://t.co/xksIrRsnIV

美国怀俄明大学32岁中国籍微生物学博士生Aili Wang，涉嫌向一名越南籍同学的茶水中投放有毒化学物质丙烯酰胺（Acrylamide），准备逃回中国时被捕。

受害者从8月开始出现手指麻木、双腿无力、失眠等症状，并发现办公室咖啡机冲泡的茶水味道异常。其妻子和大学教授随后展开调查，从咖啡机残留水中提取出63毫克含有丙烯酰胺的白色粉末。

警方安装监控后发现，Wang曾翻动受害者办公桌、逐页拍摄其研究笔记，并用自己杯中的液体冲洗对方的杯子。调查还发现，Wang涉嫌去年夏天两次通过eBay购买丙烯酰胺，事后要求平台删除账户。

受害者正在研究利用细菌将RNA送入人体细胞的新技术，涉及癌症、神经系统疾病和遗传疾病治疗，相关成果正在申请专利。指导教授Mark Gomelsky表示，Wang此前博士论文答辩失败，可能因此嫉妒成绩优异的受害者。

10月5日，Wang接受警方询问，声称自己多年未使用丙烯酰胺。次日，她在洛杉矶国际机场准备返回中国时被捕，随身携带多台笔记本电脑、外置存储设备及研究文件。

Wang目前面临最高10年监禁及1万美元罚款，怀俄明州法官已将保释金提高至150万美元。受害者目前仍有左手失去知觉、注意力难以集中、容易疲劳等神经损伤症状，能否完全康复尚不确定。

另外，目前没有证据证实Wang投毒的目的是窃取研究成果，嫉妒或科研竞争也尚未被司法机关认定为作案动机。相关指控仍有待法院审理。

text:
Anthropic just shipped a big update to the Claude Code desktop app and updated its 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗴𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴-𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲. You can ask Opus 5.5 to use it to go through your past sessions, find everything you said you'd "get to later" and then forgot, and start the ones you pick as new sessions.

While it works, it now 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗹𝗲𝗳𝘁 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲, like cart images with no set size or a checkout form missing labels. Each one becomes a card: click Start to fix it in a separate session, or Start all to open them all at once.

Hand it a few things at once and it opens a nested session for each, and each one reports back to the main session when it's done. The sidebar groups sessions into Needs input, Working and Completed. Before it stops to ask you something, it writes up the turn first, like "Images now have a width and height, all 14 tests pass. Open a PR?" To ask something on the side, type /btw and the main session keeps going.

I moved over from Codex a while back. It really is smooth.

Send this to Opus 5.5 and it'll dig up every loose end you left behind 👇

"Read this guide: https://t.co/TKFwUz0qE6

Then go through my last 20 sessions (the .jsonl logs under ~/.claude/projects/, not counting this one; the files are big, so search them by keyword and don't read them whole) and find three kinds of work I said I'd do and never did:
1. Things I said I'd "get to later", "deal with next time" or "make a note of".
2. Problems you raised while working that were outside the task at the time, like dead code, stale docs, missing tests or security risks.
3. Tasks we dropped halfway when the topic changed.

For each one, quote my exact words, say which session and which file it was in, then check the current code and cross off anything already done. Rank them by impact on the project.

Show me the list first. For each one I pick, give me a new-session card I can start with one click."

text:
AI泡沫终将破裂？这一次的冲击可能是史上最大

洛克菲勒国际董事长、突破资本（Breakout Capital）创始人，知名投资人鲁奇尔·夏尔马（Ruchir Sharma）在《外交事务》10月13日文章中预测：AI泡沫一定会爆，全世界都要为此付出惨重代价。

不到四年，三成美国人用上了AI。同一时期，美国家庭持有的财富中超过30%投在股市，比2000年互联网泡沫顶点时的27%还高。韩国股市总市值在18个月内从1.5万亿美元涨到5万亿美元以上。鲁奇尔·夏尔马认为，这就是AI泡沫。

夏尔马指出，AI已经成为全球增长的主要引擎，全球经济都在押注这条单一赛道。标普500指数前十大成分股全是AI巨头，占指数近四成，贡献了今年约一半的收益。中国增长的三分之一来自净出口，而出口主要是AI相关商品。台积电、SK海力士和三星在本地股市所占的比重，甚至高于美国科技巨头在标普500中的比重。马来西亚、墨西哥、越南以及多国矿产都被卷入AI产业链，欧洲、印度和菲律宾则被边缘化。美国数据中心建设支出同比增长约50%，其他建筑支出却下降了5%。

夏尔马用高估值、过度持有、过度投资、过度负债四项指标衡量泡沫，结果AI经济全部符合泡沫经济特征：

高估值：美国科技股15年上涨十倍，已达到历次大泡沫的标准。巨头的部分盈利来自“循环融资”：先投资AI实验室，再从实验室的采购中把钱赚回来。

过度投资：科技资本开支占GDP的6.3%，超过互联网泡沫顶峰时的6.0%，全要素生产率却几乎没有增长。

过度负债：五大云服务巨头中只有微软仍有充裕的现金流。表外租赁等安排未来十年可能再增加约3万亿美元债务。

财政托底：美国财政赤字超过GDP的6%，按作者引用的测算，撑起了这十年企业利润的一半以上。

夏尔马认为，泡沫不会因为基本面突然变化而自行破裂，而是在流动性收紧时破裂。这一次最值得警惕的，是抛售国债、推高长期利率的“债券义警”。全球债务已超过350万亿美元，约为世界经济规模的三倍，各国政府几乎没有能力救市。同时，七成美国人预计AI会减少就业，救助AI企业将遇到强大的民意阻力。

不过，AI是“好泡沫”与债务泡沫的混合体。互联网泡沫破裂后留下了互联网，这场崩盘同样会淘汰弱者，留下更强的幸存者。至于生产率红利有多大、何时兑现，现有预测从每年0.1个百分点到近2个百分点不等，可能要等上数十年。

* 请在这里查阅原文完整内容：https://t.co/TBF7iPUGBg

不到四年，三成美国人用上了AI。同一时期，美国家庭持有的财富中超过30%投在股市，比2000年互联网泡沫顶点时的27%还高。韩国股市总市值在18个月内从1.5万亿美元涨到5万亿美元以上。鲁奇尔·夏尔马认为，这就是AI泡沫。

夏尔马指出，AI已经成为全球增长的主要引擎，全球经济都在押注这条单一赛道。标普500指数前十大成分股全是AI巨头，占指数近四成，贡献了今年约一半的收益。中国增长的三分之一来自净出口，而出口主要是AI相关商品。台积电、SK海力士和三星在本地股市所占的比重，甚至高于美国科技巨头在标普500中的比重。马来西亚、墨西哥、越南以及多国矿产都被卷入AI产业链，欧洲、印度和菲律宾则被边缘化。美国数据中心建设支出同比增长约50%，其他建筑支出却下降了5%。

夏尔马用高估值、过度持有、过度投资、过度负债四项指标衡量泡沫，结果AI经济全部符合泡沫经济特征：

高估值：美国科技股15年上涨十倍，已达到历次大泡沫的标准。巨头的部分盈利来自“循环融资”：先投资AI实验室，再从实验室的采购中把钱赚回来。

过度投资：科技资本开支占GDP的6.3%，超过互联网泡沫顶峰时的6.0%，全要素生产率却几乎没有增长。

过度负债：五大云服务巨头中只有微软仍有充裕的现金流。表外租赁等安排未来十年可能再增加约3万亿美元债务。

财政托底：美国财政赤字超过GDP的6%，按作者引用的测算，撑起了这十年企业利润的一半以上。

夏尔马认为，泡沫不会因为基本面突然变化而自行破裂，而是在流动性收紧时破裂。这一次最值得警惕的，是抛售国债、推高长期利率的“债券义警”。全球债务已超过350万亿美元，约为世界经济规模的三倍，各国政府几乎没有能力救市。同时，七成美国人预计AI会减少就业，救助AI企业将遇到强大的民意阻力。

不过，AI是“好泡沫”与债务泡沫的混合体。互联网泡沫破裂后留下了互联网，这场崩盘同样会淘汰弱者，留下更强的幸存者。至于生产率红利有多大、何时兑现，现有预测从每年0.1个百分点到近2个百分点不等，可能要等上数十年。

text:
My 50 tips for using AI:

1. Data, data, data. Feed your AI as much good quality data as possible to fill in the context it hasn't got between its training data and what you want from it. With no context you'll get very generic responses.
2. Use chat history and chat memory. Build this up over time. Brain dump on it regularly. Have dedicated sessions to query the memory, fix it, and add to it.
3. Add custom instructions to fine-tune how you want it to respond and act, including the way it writes.
4. Clean up your local workspace. Add readmes to each folder to explain its context. Don't include obvious things any AI would be able to figure out.
5. Add an agents .md file to the root of your workspace. Again include context gaps only or regularly occurring mistakes. Keep it short. Use it like an if-then-else and point to an agent-docs folder with more instructions and context.
6. Use some form of task management tool, like Linear. Built-in tools are still pretty awful from my experience. Make sure to keep your task (issues) in a project. For more granular steps include checklists in your issues.
7. Use voice. Unless you're the fastest typer in the world, voice is always going to be quicker. It also lets you speak your mind. ChatGPT has great dictation, others are OK, but Copilot's particularly awful for some reason.
8. Use personal AI assistants or one session that can control all other sessions. The former is still early but is the end game for AI, get used to them. ChatGPT is really the only one that can do the latter properly at the moment.
9. When using your voice use a condenser mic that lets you talk incredibly quietly, thus not disturbing the people around you.
10. Give your AI various things, such as a master plan, principles, and an identity.
11. Ask your AI to keep a changelog and audit.
12. For schedules plan a way to have a backup so if you run out of tokens another AI can pick them up.
13. Use your AI on your mobile. It's surprising how much you can actually do. I can see a lot of us will go down to fewer and fewer and smaller and smaller screens.
14. Connect any and all relevant apps. I recommend GitHub for code work, Linear for tasks & project management, Notion for wiki and KB, Google Drive for storage and workspaces, Neon for the database, and perhaps something for video generation + image generation for Claude.
15. Use GitHub for coding. No you don't need to do any coding yourself. All control is managed by the AI.
16. And just don't be afraid of coding or building apps. You now have the power to build any app and tool you wish. There is no need to use proprietary interfaces anymore if you don't have to.
17. Ask your AI to set a schedule to review and research updates on all the tools and systems you use in your workspace. Ask it to find best practises, model releases, system card, updates, and prompting guides and ask it to suggest changes and improvements in your workspace after its review.
18. Stop doing admin. Give it to your AI. The only thing I would be wary of is managing finances. Though if you're in an area of the world that has a finance plugin such as ChatGPT in the US, use that. Other than that, from my experience, an AI can do everything else.
19. Markdown files are good but I'd recommend HTML files for explaining stuff. It's just better on the eye and gives richer content
20. Stop reading and using influencers prompts and guides (not including this one, of course 😜). They have no idea about you. You need to figure that out.
21. If you have any expertise, you are still better at that than people without that expertise so take advantage of that. AI does not make you an expert of something you are not, at least not yet or not instantly.
22. Though I'd argue coding and data analytics are solved, potentially a few other areas as well.
23. Stop paying for third-party tools and systems when AI can do that job. Ask your AI first.
24. Give it small things to do at first, then build up and up. Ask it to verify its output and check evidence. Ask it to ask you questions.
25. Give it examples and counterexamples; screenshots, files, and photos. If you're designing websites or tools, produce mockups with a relevant image generator.
26. There's no real need to start a new session nowadays but certainly create new sessions for new projects and put the AI in a new folder with project specific instructions so that session solely works on that. Use it like a worker. Keep it focused.
27. Never rely on a single model. You should have at least two chatbot plans. Use for second opinions and a backup for when one has an outage. Or just to run more work.
28. Document things you want the AI to permanently remember. Don't rely on memory and history for that.
29. Ask your agent to check your knowledge base and workspace for any conflicting info and work with it to fix it.
30. Make sure your knowledge base is easy to search, including the file names, with little explanation.
31. Build systems that last. If you're running repeatable tasks consider building a skill. I like to call these specialists.
32. Keep files and workspaces fresh. Remove any stale data.
33. Explain what "finished" and "complete" mean.
34. Prepare for mistakes. Always back up or have a way to recover.
35. AI gives you time to prototype over and over before you find your final solution. Long gone are the days of risking time on one idea for weeks or months. You can now test multiple ideas that only waste hours or days. You only need one of these to work.
36. When working with agents for the first time, start with all restrictions on and slowly but surely give it more and more freedom. They work better with fewer restrictions.
37. Only use AI if you need intelligence. Else use automation. Remember AI is still not 100% accurate, or 100% hallucination-free. Nor is it cheap. Tokens are precious.
38. So ask the AI to use scripts, formulas, and schedules where it can.
39. Schedules allow you to run your AI while you're not even at your desk, such as overnight, at weekends, and on all holidays. Set exactly what you want it to do: some AI can set fairly dynamic schedules (such as one piece of work during the week and a different piece of work during the weekend) or are reactive depending on the results
40. Ask your AI to run parallel sessions to get more work done quicker. Or if you're not using a personal AI assistant or orchestration, run multiple sessions at once yourself.
41. Use desktop apps for your AI. They give you so much more than the web versions.
42. Speak to your AI a lot. Most AI are powerful enough out of the box that a lot of prompting techniques are now dead. Talk to it like you talk to a person to get the best out of it.
43. AI is like a work colleague, be it one without context. Treat it as such.
44. Get it to question your assumptions, identify weaknesses, and present alternatives. Ask for pushback
45. Always fact-check important claims and ask for sources and dates.
46. Check what it can actually access. Don't presume what it tells you is correct.
47. No need to wait for the perfect use case. Just give it a problem right in front of you now.
48. Watch for silent failures such as schedules breaking.
49. This advice will get outdated very quickly. Always keep up to date with the latest news and techniques.
50. My top tip is just to start using it. The earlier the better. You'll start to understand how they work and their pros and cons. You'll also start to build up context, memories, and history, which are hugely vital.

We're at the stage where we are now delegators and supervisors, get the AI to do most of the work as long as you give it good instructions at the start, check it thoroughly at the end and guide it in the middle.

Save this before you scale your team

text:
Went back to codex desktop today to do some tax prep stuff and holy hell the ChatGPT desktop app is falling apart 

There's so much here I like and want to use, but it's such a slow, janky, incoherent mess it's impossible

The new "spaces" feature is actually amazing. Such a good idea that I've been building a lot of my video pipelines around, the only problem is that buggy and the UX is a dumpster fire

It seriously feels like there are 5 companies all working on their own products who have to ship them all together in the chatgpt desktop app while not being allowed to talk to each other

Go back and look at Dev day, they shipped 30+ features. Almost all of these are dope and useful. The problem is you haven't heard of 80% of them and it's all just floating around in this blob that's chatgpt

This stuff is hard, I don't envy the position they're in. You have to keep shipping as fast as possible so you don't fall behind, but you also need time to polish and organize things. And this has to be coordinated across a bunch of teams and dozens of people and hundreds (thousands) of agents. 

I could go through all the specific issues but 1) it'd take too long and 2) anyone who uses it already knows most of these (very laggy, sidebar sucks, features are too hidden, spaces "tabs" system is a mess, etc.)

Codex desperately needs a dictator with an actual coherent vision

If you're tired of 3rd parties sharing your email address here's a prompt to give your Grok @bot (or any other agent):

Remove my personal and contact info from B2B contact-data sellers and people-search brokers (e.g. Apollo, ZoomInfo, RocketReach, Lusha, ContactOut, Seamless AI, Hunter, Clearbit, Cognism, Kaspr, SignalHire, People Data Labs, LeadIQ, Adapt io, UpLead, plus any others common in my country).

1. Ask me for my name, the emails I use, and where I live, then look up each provider's current official opt-out route on their own site.
2. Write a short deletion and opt-out request that cites the privacy law that applies where I live (e.g. GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA or another US state law, PIPEDA, the Australian Privacy Act). Request deletion of all my data, an end to any sale or sharing, deletion of linked profiles, and written confirmation.
3. Show me the emails as drafts from my own email account. Send them only after I approve.
4. Fill out web forms for providers that don't accept email.
5. Give me a list of what was sent, what's still pending, and any confirmation links I need to click.
6. Offer to repeat this every quarter.

Any other ideas welcome in the replies, tired of getting this spam.

text:
How AI for the enterprise is evolving, from owning a task to owning an outcome:

1. Assistant: handles one task in seconds, like sending a follow-up email. Companies pay for it out of their software budget.

2. Agent: handles one interaction in minutes, like a customer's refund call. It takes on work people used to do, so it gets paid for out of the labor budget.

3. Long-running agent: works toward a goal for weeks or months, like getting an injured client the biggest settlement possible. Because it owns the result, the company selling it can price on the outcome it delivers.

Full piece from a16z's @dhaber on long-running agents in high-value customer journeys: https://t.co/aHaatcizcd

Google AI Ultra $200/月，大部分人只拿来用 Gemini，其实里面还塞了每月 2000 个 Colab 算力单位（CU）。
按 Colab 自己的零售价（$9.99/100 CU），这部分单独就值 $199.8，相当于订阅费又送了你一遍。

我把这 2000 CU 换算成了能跑多少视频、图片、克隆语音和 GLM。结果有的项目香到离谱，有的还不如直接调 API 👇

2/ 先算预算
Premium GPU 只有 Ultra 能用。Colab 里选 G4，就是 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell，96GB 显存，社区实测 8.71 CU/小时。

2000 ÷ 8.71 = 229.6 小时/月
平均每天 7.6 小时，开着后台跑都行
（A100 80GB 是 7.52 CU/h，能跑 266 小时，但少了 16GB 显存，后面 GLM 那个就塞不下了）

3/ 视频①：LTX-2.3（Lightricks，22B，开源，自带音效）
同款 RTX PRO 6000 实测：蒸馏版出一条 10 秒、1344×768、带声音的视频大约 57 秒。
→ 每小时 63 条
→ 一个月 14,500 条，合计 40 小时视频素材
→ 按 LTX 官方 API 1080p Fast 档 $0.40/条粗算，等价 $5,800（分辨率比 1080p 低一档，看个量级）

4/ 但没人一次就出片，按真实工作流算：
一条 1 分钟短视频 = 6 个 10 秒镜头 × 每个抽 4 次 = 24 次生成
≈ 23 分钟 GPU ≈ 3.3 CU

→ 一个月 604 条 1 分钟成片
→ 每天 20 条，日更 5 个号都够
5/ 视频②：要画质天花板就上 Wan 2.2 A14B（阿里，27B MoE）
720p 5 秒，H100 上都要 10-12 分钟一条，G4 我按 15 分钟保守算：

→ 一个月 918 条，共 76 分钟视频
→ 按 4 次抽 1 条能用：230 个镜头，19 分钟成片
结论：Wan 做精品镜头，量产还得 LTX
6/ 图片：Qwen-Image-2512（阿里，20B，Apache 2.0，中文字渲染最强那个）
1328×1328 满 50 步，约 80 秒一张 → 每月 10,333 张，每天 344 张
挂 Lightning LoRA 跑 8 步，约 8 秒一张 → 每月 10.3 万张，每天 3,444 张

只要快：Z-Image Turbo（6B），1536×1536 约 9 秒一张 → 每月 9.2 万张
（速度按 RTX 5090 实测换算，G4 跟 5090 是同一颗芯片、核心还更多，这是保守值）
7/ 克隆你自己的声音：Fish Audio S2 Pro（4B + 400M，开源权重）
录 10-30 秒自己的声音就能克隆，中文是一档支持语言，官方报告 Seed-TTS 中文 WER 0.54%，开源闭源里最低。

官方 H200 单路 RTF 0.34，G4 带宽低，我按慢 2 倍算（RTF≈0.68）：
→ 1 小时 GPU 出 1.47 小时音频，一个月 338 小时
→ 每天一期 15 分钟播客，一个月只花 44 CU，占 2.2%
→ 一本 10 小时有声书 ≈ 59 CU
（S2 是 Fish Audio Research License，商用要另谈授权）

8/ 跑大模型：GLM-5.3-Flash（智谱 8 月开源，320B 总参 / 18B 激活，MIT）
先泼盆冷水：FP8 原版 300+GB，单卡根本塞不下。DeepSeek V4 Flash（284B）也一样，官方权重 160+GB。

能跑的办法：社区 2-bit 量化版 AJ-IQ2_XXS，87GB，刚好整个塞进 G4 的 96GB。
9/ RTX PRO 6000 上全显存实测：
空上下文 69.9 tok/s → 每月 5,780 万 token
8K 上下文 52.7 tok/s → 每月 4,360 万
32K 上下文（写代码 agent 的常态）31.7 tok/s → 每月 2,620 万

折下来每天 87 万到 190 万 token。

10/ 但说句实话：
同样 4,360 万 token，走 GLM-5.3-Flash 官方 API（输出 $0.50/M）只要 $22 左右。
而且 2-bit 版跟原版的 top-1 一致率只有 73%，不是满血。
所以 Colab 跑大模型不是为了省钱，是为了数据不出门、能微调、能随便改。纯要 token，直接调 API。
11/ 总结：$200 Ultra 里的 2000 CU，每月能换（每项单独用满，不能叠加）：
🎬 LTX-2.3：14,500 条 10 秒视频，或 604 条 1 分钟成片
🎞 Wan 2.2：918 条 720p 精品镜头
🖼 Qwen-Image-2512：1 万张满血图，或 10 万张快速图
🎙 Fish S2 Pro：338 小时你自己声音的音频
🧠 GLM-5.3-Flash 2-bit：2,600 万到 5,800 万 token

视频和图片是真香，大模型就当玩具。

12/ 几个坑：

CU 费率是社区实测，Google 没公开，会浮动
G4/H100 高峰期经常连不上，Ultra 有优先但不保证

Colab 磁盘是临时的，每次开机都要重新下模型（GLM 一次 87GB）
$100 档的 Ultra 是 1000 CU，以上全部减半

text:
An engineer 𝘁𝘄𝗼 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗮 𝗯𝗶𝗴 𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗷𝗼𝗯 already owns several projects. Their manager set up a few 1:1s to find out how the AI dev workflow behind that is built.

The engineer leans on 5 very short prompts and calls them 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹'𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗰𝘂𝘁𝘀. Sometimes one line does the work of thousands. Each one names a single method. The model saw plenty of papers and code on these methods in training, so naming one is often enough.
→ When an API is slow and the plan is already "add a Redis cache," have it work from first principles to find whether the time goes to SQL, the network or repeated work. An index might be all it takes
→ When you review a plan or code, ask for an adversarial review that hunts for counterexamples to the core assumptions. Say you want a distributed lock: it'll first ask whether making the endpoint idempotent would do
→ If you shipped three optimizations at once and the endpoint got faster, have it design an ablation test that pulls them apart. It might turn out the index alone took it from 800ms to 120ms
→ When the agent piles up Kafka, Redis and distributed locks, add "review this design with Occam's razor." Often a single transaction with a unique index is enough
→ When a service class hits 2,000 lines, ask it to "review the responsibility boundaries for high cohesion and low coupling, and don't split things just to split them"

In Claude Code, once Opus 5.5 has written the plan and before it touches any code, send this as your next message 👇
"Re-analyze this from first principles and run an adversarial review of the current plan. Core mechanisms must be validated with ablation tests. Follow Occam's razor in the design, and keep the code highly cohesive and loosely coupled."

quotedTweet.text:
Six Thinking Hats came out 40 years ago, and plenty of companies still run meetings with it. I used Opus 5.5 to turn it into 𝟲 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀, basically my own team of advisors.

Edward de Bono once wrote, "The main difficulty of thinking is confusion. We try to do too much at once. Emotions, information, logic, hope, and creativity all crowd in on us. It is like juggling with too many balls." His fix was six hats in six colors. Wear the white hat and you only talk facts. Wear the black hat and you only look for risks.

⚪ white-hat (medium): the facts
↓ same facts to all four, at the same time
🔴 red-hat (low): gut call
🟡 yellow-hat (medium): the case for it
⚫ black-hat (high): risks
🟢 green-hat (high): options, tried in its own worktree
↓ all five outputs
🔵 blue-hat (xhigh): one plan

To set up the hats, send this straight to Claude Code 👇

"Set up Edward de Bono's Six Thinking Hats as six subagents in .claude/agents/. Create them, then stop. Don't use them yet.

- white-hat (effort: medium, read-only): facts only. List what we know and what's missing, and mark each point verified or guessed.
- red-hat (effort: low, read-only): gut reactions in a few lines. No justification needed.
- yellow-hat (effort: medium, read-only): the strongest case for doing it and the value it creates.
- black-hat (effort: high, read-only): risks and what could break. Point them out, don't fix anything.
- green-hat (effort: high, isolation: worktree): alternatives and new options. It may try them in its own worktree. Keep scratch files inside it, and end by listing the files it changed and where the worktree is.
- blue-hat (effort: xhigh, read-only): reads everyone's output and returns one plan: the decision, next steps, open questions.

Give each hat its matching color where Claude Code has one. If this project had no .claude/agents/ folder before, remind me to restart Claude Code when you're done."

To use them 👇

"Use the six hat subagents in .claude/agents/ on the decision below. Call each hat by its agent type. If a type isn't available, stop and tell me to restart Claude Code. Don't fall back to general-purpose. Run white-hat first. Then run red-hat, yellow-hat, black-hat and green-hat in parallel, each with white-hat's facts. Last, give blue-hat the full output from all five. Show me the plan before changing anything on the main branch.

Decision: [one sentence on what you're stuck on]"

Once they're split into subagents, four hats think at the same time. A full round on Opus 5.5 took 𝟴.𝟱 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝘂𝘁𝗲𝘀. Really efficient.

Six Thinking Hats came out 40 years ago, and plenty of companies still run meetings with it. I used Opus 5.5 to turn it into 𝟲 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀, basically my own team of advisors.

Edward de Bono once wrote, "The main difficulty of thinking is confusion. We try to do too much at once. Emotions, information, logic, hope, and creativity all crowd in on us. It is like juggling with too many balls." His fix was six hats in six colors. Wear the white hat and you only talk facts. Wear the black hat and you only look for risks.

⚪ white-hat (medium): the facts
↓ same facts to all four, at the same time
🔴 red-hat (low): gut call
🟡 yellow-hat (medium): the case for it
⚫ black-hat (high): risks
🟢 green-hat (high): options, tried in its own worktree
↓ all five outputs
🔵 blue-hat (xhigh): one plan

To set up the hats, send this straight to Claude Code 👇

"Set up Edward de Bono's Six Thinking Hats as six subagents in .claude/agents/. Create them, then stop. Don't use them yet.

- white-hat (effort: medium, read-only): facts only. List what we know and what's missing, and mark each point verified or guessed.
- red-hat (effort: low, read-only): gut reactions in a few lines. No justification needed.
- yellow-hat (effort: medium, read-only): the strongest case for doing it and the value it creates.
- black-hat (effort: high, read-only): risks and what could break. Point them out, don't fix anything.
- green-hat (effort: high, isolation: worktree): alternatives and new options. It may try them in its own worktree. Keep scratch files inside it, and end by listing the files it changed and where the worktree is.
- blue-hat (effort: xhigh, read-only): reads everyone's output and returns one plan: the decision, next steps, open questions.

Give each hat its matching color where Claude Code has one. If this project had no .claude/agents/ folder before, remind me to restart Claude Code when you're done."

To use them 👇

"Use the six hat subagents in .claude/agents/ on the decision below. Call each hat by its agent type. If a type isn't available, stop and tell me to restart Claude Code. Don't fall back to general-purpose. Run white-hat first. Then run red-hat, yellow-hat, black-hat and green-hat in parallel, each with white-hat's facts. Last, give blue-hat the full output from all five. Show me the plan before changing anything on the main branch.

Decision: [one sentence on what you're stuck on]"

Once they're split into subagents, four hats think at the same time. A full round on Opus 5.5 took 𝟴.𝟱 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝘂𝘁𝗲𝘀. Really efficient.

quotedTweet.text:
聊一下趋势交易和日内交易的区别
想到啥说啥，没有打草稿

趋势交易，我从2020年开始做日线趋势，这个需要大周期配合，买在起涨点一直持有到趋势被反转。比如2020年BTC我是12000进场的，一直拿到6万。当时本金只有1200U，持仓半年一波自由

趋势转折最简单的判断方法是均线密集横盘之后重新跳上均线。难点在耐心，几年一次机会，这一次机会需要你多次进场打脸再进场再打脸，你要是受得了，那趋势必然会给你发红包

接下来欢迎来到史诗难度的持仓阶段，这时候需要屏蔽所有交易相关的社交媒体，他们只会给你带来噪音。你要相信自己，等了几年的机会你不会看错的。

你要知道上涨是越来越快的，下跌是越来越慢的，当你看到铺天盖地的消息在讨论你的标的，价格加速上涨的时候，你就要格外谨慎了，别问我怎么去量化铺天盖地这个词。BRO，信我，你不是吊毛，你一定会知道怎么去衡量这个尺度

你不必买在底部，只需要买在中继就行，从趋势交易来看，你买在的底部，一定会拿不到主升浪。往往买在中继大概率会拿到主升浪。行情是公平的，底部进场拿趋势往往会不尽人意。

日内交易：
我从今年2月开始学习日内交易，目前是周内波段。聊一下我感悟最深的几点
1，日内交易并不是每天都交易，而是进场后持有到日线收盘前或者是持有某个重要的时间段开盘，比如LZ进场持有到NY开盘

2，心态是日内的交易最大的敌人，别给我说趋势交易也考验心态，你放心，日内交易的心态管理的难度是趋势交易的几倍几十倍

3，非常非常的消耗你的精力，经常会很疲惫，心态起伏巨大

4，日内交易的复利我觉得是个伪命题，并不是每次2%的仓位管理都会生效的。为什么，因为你是人，是人就无发保证心态一直恒定在一个很稳定的区间，顶级交易员静心大师给我聊过这样一句话，日内交易就用固定止损金额，别用百分比仓位管理。有利润就提现，不然亏起来特别快。现在我深以为然

5，只做固定模式，弯弯绕绕的行情你别做

6，非常依赖身体状态，状态交易就好，状态差交易就差，你会顺一段时间，记住当你觉得很顺的时候，停手一周，不然马上会大回撤，百试不爽。

我发现经过8个月的日内交易训练，我觉得我并不适合做日内，性格不符。我不喜欢天天坐着看盘，所以我一直在尝试把流动性策略和趋势交易结合。比如现在的原油就是我第一次尝试的品种，效果相当满意。

好处是我可以在趋势的中继形态假突破就进场，不必等到站上均线，因为关键点位的价格反应至关重要，有反应就会可以进场，进场就会有利润，会非常快。

今天就说这么多

卧槽，REA 还是太超标了啊，这下人人都是 Claude 设计总监了！

一直觉得 Claude 的前端特别丝滑
但我不是专业前端，用 Claude 自己复刻也一直做不出那个味儿

刚用 REA 把 Claude Desktop 底裤都扒光了，才发现 UI 藏了这么多细节
啥吸附、过渡、咬合、贝塞尔曲线，之前从来没考虑过🤣

1️⃣在暗色模式下，白字黑底在人眼的视觉上上会因视网膜光渗效应产生光晕发散，视觉上感觉比浅色模式粗10%~15%
所以 Claude 把字重从 500 / 600 减到了 460 / 560
两个主题下看起来粗细完全一致

2️⃣正文绝不让一个字单独占一行
会自动把倒数第二个词拉下来一起换行

3️⃣回答的字是一个个「晕开」出来的
每个字从模糊到清晰只要 90ms，一个接一个
难怪看着那么舒服

text:
Until recently, AI agents mostly handled short tasks, like one support call or one email. Now they can stay on a job for weeks or months.

That matters for "relay race" work that runs through a long chain of people.

Every handoff in that chain is a chance for something to fall through: a slow callback, a dropped follow-up, lost context.

Take a personal injury case. Today it moves from intake to investigation to the demand letter, with different people at each step. A single case agent can work it from the first call to settlement, chasing witnesses, records, and bills, and keeping the client and attorney updated along the way.

The same idea applies to processes like mortgages, insurance claims, and enterprise sales.

Because the agent owns the end result, the company selling it can charge on the outcome (a closed loan, a settled case, a signed deal) and move past pricing on the labor it saves (paralegal hours, call center seats).

Full piece from a16z's @dhaber on long-running agents in high-value customer journeys: https://t.co/aHaatcizcd

text:
昨天因为我前天早上发挥低素质能力精确优雅地运用 6 个「操你妈」和 2 个「你妈死了」辱骂了几个对我阴阳怪气恶意抹黑者，导致被他们举报后因违反推特规定我的推特账号被封禁 12 个小时。所以有些事情没来得及过来补充。现在解封后特地来补充一下。

当时关于为啥相对激进地采用这种工作流，主要是因为我在一开始设计 Magpie 的时候，就是想把 Magpie 做为一个运行在用户本地的 Agent 基础设施，让它作为一个 bridge 去连接散落在用户本地电脑上的各式各样的 Agent 和越来越多难以维护的大模型订阅供应商，解决两者没打通导致每个人每个月手里浪费大量订阅的 Token 甚至因为供应商绑定导致无法切换 Agent 等等一系列问题。

但挑战也随之而来，因为我用过的 Agent 就那么几个，听说和订阅过的供应商也就那么几家，可是这个世界上的 Agent 和供应商都太多了，而且相互之间各种差异，每个人都有自己独特的偏好，更何况每个 Agent 都有自己千奇百怪独有的配置和设计，供应商自己也有千奇百怪的订阅花活儿，所以一旦把产品交付出去，那么我注定无法应对所有人的各式各样的 Agent 和供应商的支持需求，所以 Magpie 在早期它注定就应该是 UGC 的，也就是用户提需求我来帮其实现。所以我才自然而然地打造了这一套 Agent loop 工作流。

但是 Agent driven 的 UGC 也是有风险的，比如很多人在吐槽的 Magpie 看起来一直在堆砌功能在产品观上没有克制，以及因为要快速交付获得反馈导致发版过快让人觉得不靠谱，其实事情一直都在起变化，最近这一切都在极大地缓解，首先现在 Magpie 已经把 Provider 和 Agent 分别都插件化了，这个解耦导致以后相关它们的新的支持和修复都不需要动 Magpie 产品本身。其次，Magpie 下一步就是在保留最核心功能框架的基础上把所有的功能包括 UI 都插件化，让 Magpie 本身变得轻盈的同时不阻碍它做迭代和功能扩展。

text:
基于ai目前发展的情况来看，其对社会的深刻影响，最可能的情况既不会是完全平等的“哈耶克式乌托邦”，也不会是纯粹极权的“数字利维坦”，而会演变为一种“倒金字塔式的新封建分层”（Neo-Feudal Layering）。

这种结构是波普尔的演化试错、哈耶克的边缘自发秩序、以及彼得·蒂尔的垄断现实主义在不同物理层面的强制组合。

最可能出现的发展格局可以清晰地划分为三个层级（如图）：

顶层：算力与能源的“新封建垄断”，因为前沿模型（Frontier Models）的训练成本并不会因为“开源扩散”而下降，反而因为逼近物理极限（千兆瓦级核能供应、定制光互连、数十万张高阶算力集群）而变成只有国家意志和极少数万亿级寡头才能承受的“曼哈顿工程”。
数字租金与主权结盟：顶层寡头不再需要直接控制每一个终端应用，他们成为提供“底层智能基质（Intelligence Utility）”的数字领主。如同彼得·蒂尔所预言的，这一层级彻底消灭了盲目竞争，转而与国家安全机器（正如 Palantir、五角大楼的合作模式）深度绑定，垄断了最致命的现实干涉能力（军工、地缘情报、生化合成与主权计算）。

中层：中产科层崩解与“微型哈耶克网络”的繁荣（哈耶克的部分实现）
知识中介的死亡：过去依赖“信息不对称”和“标准化流程”维系的中层机构（如法律合规、初级金融分析、常规软件外包、甚至中层管理）将大面积瓦解。
自发秩序的爆发：拥有 AI 杠杆的个体或 3-5 人的极小团队，能够调动过去数百人才能完成的生产力。正如哈耶克所洞见的，分散在个体身上的局部审美、非标需求和人际信任被彻底激活，催生出极其庞大、动态且灵活的“超级自由职业/微型企业生态网”。
但是，这是一个“没有定价权的繁荣”：这些微型主体在应用层激烈竞争（完全契合蒂尔“竞争是属于失败者的”论断），最终挤干了所有过剩利润，其创造的剩余价值大部分通过“API 调用费、云基础设施租金”被抽水至顶层。

底层：认知环境恶化与民主纠错机制的钝化（波普尔最担忧的挑战）
事实的“相对主义灾难”：波普尔的开放社会建立在“理性批判与事实证伪”之上。但当本地部署的开源 AI 能够以零成本生成完美逼真的图文声像时，公众的共同现实基础被彻底腐蚀。
部落化退缩：面对算法生成的内容洪流，人类为了自我保护，会加速退回由血缘、狂热信仰或封闭圈子组成的“现代部落”。理性批判让位于身份认同，这正是波普尔一生都在警惕的封闭社会的回归。

第一阶段：白领“阶梯式出清”与成本套利（当下正在发生）

开源模型的性能逐步逼近前几代闭源模型，引发“平权化”的普遍乐观假象。

第二阶段：主权与巨头的“高墙筑起”（未来 1-3 年）
随着前沿智能突破到能够自主执行现实物理任务（网络攻击、材料与病原体推演），以“国家安全”和“生物安全”为名的监管全面收紧。
前沿算力受到类似核材料级别的出口管制与物理监控，底层的“物理垄断”与民间的“应用平权”正式完成法律和制度上的割席。

第三阶段：制度的“试错式硬着陆”（未来 3–7 年）
伴随着高失业，传统以“劳动所得税”为支柱的现代福利国家财政体系陷入停滞。

quotedTweet.text:
it's easy to fall into the trap of micromanaging your agents instead of correcting the environment that shapes its behavior. 

pstack 0.15.9 now ships a new /correct skill: if you keep correcting agents for the same mistakes, it finds the pattern and fixes it with architecture, types, and checks.

i like to imagine that commits rapidly flowing into the codebase are like a bonsai tree rapidly growing in whatever direction it pleases. what you want to do is not to give in to the chaos, but tame it intentionally with the right constraints

0.15.9 also has improvements to:
• /architect: now includes instructions on designing agent friendly architecture
• a new /benchmark-checklist skill based on @brendangregg's benchmarking checklist

here's a prompt you can give to grok bot to start architecting a better codebase with pstack: 

/poteto-mode create a new Project agent to refactor and rearchitect my repo so that our architecture is more agent friendly. it should use both the /correct and /architect skill to look through past commits and find the most common pitfalls that agents fall into, whether its with code quality, performance, or bugs. if relevant you can also use the /recall skill to find past conversations for context. it should make a high level plan for me to review. it should also answer its own open questions by prototyping rather than defer to me. come back to me with a plan backed by real data. once i approve the plan, use either the stack or full autopilot playbook (ask me which i want) to execute

text:
A follow-up to my earlier comment on the Koberda and Kontorovich dialogue about the future of mathematics under strong AI.

My core suggestion was that mathematics may follow the path of sports: cognitive fitness for many, a highly competitive professional tier for a few, and funding of the professional infrastructure by the AI labs that benefit most from the talent and independent judgment it produces. Pressing the idea against its strongest objections raised the collective action questions that follow.

Free-riding is real: big clubs, or labs, can simply hire talent others trained. Football solved this not by goodwill but by formal rules: training compensation and solidarity payments on transfers, homegrown quotas, and contracts that bind young players to the club that develops them. AI equivalents are straightforward: industry-sponsored PhDs with service commitments, a payment when a funded researcher joins a competitor, or a levy into a common fund. Winner-take-most dynamics can help rather than hurt. A dominant lab that captures most of the returns from a healthy mathematical ecosystem has a private reason to underwrite it, much as AT&T underwrote Bell Labs.

Independence is harder. The practical answer is arm's length structures: labs contributing to independent foundations that make grants without lab control, alongside continued public and philanthropic money. A mixed model protects independence better than any single source.

On scale, demand for cognitive fitness can sustain the broad base of undergraduates and recreational mathematics, much as members sustain gyms. Labs mainly need to fund the elite tier. The vulnerable middle, graduate programs and mid-tier research positions, still requires public support. But a hollowed-out middle eventually starves the elite pipeline, so labs have reason to want, and lobby for, that support too.

Narrowing is the other risk. Funding only what looks useful today misses black swans. Neural networks were kept alive for decades by a handful of researchers in an unfashionable corner; the payoff was later enormous and widely shared. A lab that funds only fashionable areas is betting the next breakthrough arrives where it expects, which history says is a losing bet. And the lab that funds the decisive corner rarely captures the full return, as Bell Labs found with the transistor. The rational response is not narrow, firm-specific funding but a pooled, independent fund that keeps the field broad on everyone's behalf.

A plausible equilibrium is a smaller but still broad field, provided the mechanisms that protect breadth are in place. Coordination still needs a proposer, and mathematicians are unusually well suited for that role: they understand the game theory, they know which forms of breadth have mattered historically, and they have the most to lose if no one acts. The incentives and the institutional templates exist. What remains is to write the concrete proposal, with a levy formula, a governance sketch and a pilot structure, so that labs, foundations and public agencies have something specific to react to.

quotedTweet.text:
Really enjoyed the format, and I think the Dialectical Understanding Axiom gets to the heart of the matter.

I suspect mathematics will follow the path of sports. We no longer need strong men and women for most physical work, yet gyms are full, because physical strength and exercise have value beyond their economic utility. Mathematical training may become cognitive fitness in much the same way.

At the professional level, it may look more like tennis: fierce competition, fewer positions at the top, enormously unequal rewards, and young people still willing to pursue excellence despite the odds. Eloquence versus depth is a genuine selection problem, but hardly a new one. Other fields have considerable experience distinguishing performance from competence, however imperfectly.

But who pays for the professional infrastructure?

My candidate is the AI industry itself. Lean can verify a proof of a formal statement, but it cannot establish that the intended theorem was formalized correctly or that the result matters. Even if AI eventually becomes better at all of these tasks, preserving independent human mathematical judgment remains valuable.

The AI labs are among the greatest beneficiaries of mathematical research. Like professional football clubs, they have an interest in funding the academies that produce talent, rather than merely buying finished players. And like football, they may need rules that reward training, since each lab would rather hire mathematicians than develop them.

That suggests why the Funding Premise might not materialize: AI companies may become major sponsors of mathematical education and research, sustaining the very human expertise that their technology is making less necessary for routine production.

Of course, whether their collective interest translates into actual funding, and whether experts funded by the labs can stay independent of them, is another question.

Curious whether you see the economics developing this way.

The vulnerable middle, graduate programs and mid-tier research positions, still requires public support. But a hollowed-out middle eventually starves the elite pipeline, so labs have reason to want, and lobby for, that support too.

Narrowing is the other risk. Funding only what looks useful today misses black swans. Neural networks were kept alive for decades by a handful of researchers in an unfashionable corner; the payoff was later enormous and widely shared. A lab that funds only fashionable areas is betting the next breakthrough arrives where it expects, which history says is a losing bet. And the lab that funds the decisive corner rarely captures the full return, as Bell Labs found with the transistor. The rational response is not narrow, firm-specific funding but a pooled, independent fund that keeps the field broad on everyone's behalf.

A plausible equilibrium is a smaller but still broad field, provided the mechanisms that protect breadth are in place. Coordination still needs a proposer, and mathematicians are unusually well suited for that role: they understand the game theory, they know which forms of breadth have mattered historically, and they have the most to lose if no one acts. The incentives and the institutional templates exist. What remains is to write the concrete proposal, with a levy formula, a governance sketch and a pilot structure, so that labs, foundations and public agencies have something specific to react to.

result.text:
Really enjoyed the format, and I think the Dialectical Understanding Axiom gets to the heart of the matter.

I suspect mathematics will follow the path of sports. We no longer need strong men and women for most physical work, yet gyms are full, because physical strength and exercise have value beyond their economic utility. Mathematical training may become cognitive fitness in much the same way.

At the professional level, it may look more like tennis: fierce competition, fewer positions at the top, enormously unequal rewards, and young people still willing to pursue excellence despite the odds. Eloquence versus depth is a genuine selection problem, but hardly a new one. Other fields have considerable experience distinguishing performance from competence, however imperfectly.

But who pays for the professional infrastructure?

My candidate is the AI industry itself. Lean can verify a proof of a formal statement, but it cannot establish that the intended theorem was formalized correctly or that the result matters. Even if AI eventually becomes better at all of these tasks, preserving independent human mathematical judgment remains valuable.

The AI labs are among the greatest beneficiaries of mathematical research. Like professional football clubs, they have an interest in funding the academies that produce talent, rather than merely buying finished players. And like football, they may need rules that reward training, since each lab would rather hire mathematicians than develop them.

That suggests why the Funding Premise might not materialize: AI companies may become major sponsors of mathematical education and research, sustaining the very human expertise that their technology is making less necessary for routine production.

Of course, whether their collective interest translates into actual funding, and whether experts funded by the labs can stay independent of them, is another question.

Curious whether you see the economics developing this way.

text:
I love studying history because it’s such fertile ground of inspiration for my own fiction 😊 and one of my favorite lesser-known figures is the beautiful and incorrigible Alcibiades 🇬🇷, the traitor of traitors! 

Alcibiades was an Athenian nobleman born during the peak of Athenian power, living during the time of its generation-long conflict with Sparta, the Peloponnesian War. He inherited substantial wealth and had family ties of guardianship to Pericles himself!

Wealthy, charismatic, and (apparently) gorgeous, Alcibiades was always a larger than life character in Athenian politics. There are so many stories and anecdotes about him preserved by later historians like Plutarch. One even suggesting an intimate friendship with Socrates, with whom he served in the military!

Alcibiades wanted glory, and pushed for Athens to launch a massive invasion of Sicily to take down the rival city of Syracuse. This invasion later ended up being an absolute disaster for Athens, with almost its entire fleet destroyed and thousands of men either killed or taken prisoner and enslaved. But before that could happen, Alcibiades was charged with the crime of blasphemy and ordered to return to Athens to face charges.

Alcibiades, being Alcibiades, said “to Hades with that”, and became a fugitive. Athens was furious, and sentenced him to death in absentia. What was Alcibiades to do?

Easy. Alcibiades fled Athens and traveled to Sparta, offering his aid to King Agis! His former arch enemy! Alcibiades gave the Spartans strategic advice on how to profit from Athens’ misfortune in Sicily. A shameless traitor, Alcibiades was eventually forced to flee Sparta only after getting caught in affair with King Agis’s wife! The Spartan king was furious that his own traitor had betrayed him! 😂 

So, where did he go next? To Persia, another ancient enemy of his people! Alcibiades befriended the Persian satrap Tissaphernes and, once again, gave shrewd strategic tips as an advisor: “Don’t fight Greeks directly. Let Athens and Sparta fight each other. Nobody hates Greeks more than other Greeks.”

His end-game, of course, was purely selfish. He wanted Athens to be desperate enough so that he could use his Persian connections as an argument “only I can keep you safe”, and thereby get his death sentence forgiven. His same home city that exiled him would be clamoring for him to come back.

Did Alcibiades feel any shame? Later historians always portray him as a narcissistic ego maniac, but the worst kind, the one who’s genuinely likable and so charming you almost forget why you’re mad at him!

Nothing lasts forever. Alcibiades met a gruesome end, but I think we can still see his personality type in the world today!

There's one sentence that gets late invoices paid faster than any "FINAL NOTICE" ever will.

It's not a threat.
It's not a late fee.

It's actually the opposite. And almost no business owner uses it 👇

First, you need to understand why people don't pay you.

It's not because they're broke.
It's not because they're bad people.

It's one of two reasons:

1. They forgot.
2. Something about the job bugged them, and they'd rather ghost you than say it.

Reason 1 is easy. Reminders.
Reason 2 is where your money is stuck.

Because a customer who's slightly unhappy doesn't complain.
They just... don't pay.
And you never find out why.

So here's the sentence:

"If something about the job wasn't right, tell me and I'll make it right."

That's it.

It turns a silent ghost into a conversation.
And a conversation almost always ends in a payment.

Now here's how to put it on autopilot so you never chase an invoice again:

Day 0: "Thanks for having us out today. Here's your invoice: [link]. Takes 30 seconds by card."

Day 3: "Quick reminder, your invoice is ready whenever you are: [link]."

Day 7: "Just checking this didn't get buried: [link]. If something about the job wasn't right, tell me and I'll make it right."

Day 14: "Your invoice is now 2 weeks past due. Can you take care of it today? If you need to split it up, reply and we'll set that up."

See where the magic sentence sits?
Day 7. Right when silence starts turning into "never."

Load these into the automatic reminders in QuickBooks, Jobber, Housecall Pro or Square.
Set it once.
Never send an awkward "hey just following up 😅" text again.

This is one system from my 5-book playbook "The Autopilot Owner."

Like this post and I'll DM it to you. 📩

硅谷教父、16z 联合创始人、网景浏览器创始人马克·安德森最近把过去 25 年现代经济最大的荒谬一刀切开了，

为什么所有跟芯片、代码相关的科技硬件价格全在崩盘，而房子、医疗和大学学费这老三样，反而贵到了普通人倾家荡产也够不着的地步。

他在访谈里给出了一个极其残酷的底层账本，
过去四分之一个世纪，凡是科技能够自由渗透和竞争的领域，成本全部坍缩：电视机、电脑硬件、电子元件几乎全变成了白菜价。

但构筑中产安全感的三大核心支柱，离好工作近的房子、全家人的优质医疗、送孩子进好学校的门票，价格曲线全部一路飙上天。

表面上看是普遍通胀，本质上是一个写在政策里的致命死循环：
第一步，通过严苛的土地分区法规卡死住房供给，通过极其保守的认证机制卡死优质高校与医疗机构的牌照供给。

第二步，面对价格暴涨带来的巨大社会压力，政府不肯松绑供给，反而转头去疯狂补贴需求，发放天量低息学贷、住房补贴和医保兜底。

当供给被人为死死焊在铁板上，任何砸向需求的补贴，最终都会一分不差地直接变成资产拥有者涨价的燃料。

说白了，凡是允许技术自由重构的地方，一切都在疯狂变便宜；凡是用行政高墙锁死供给、又试图靠撒钱补贴需求的地方，穷人永远被收割在天价账单里。

换作是你，你觉得未来十年，AI 能不能彻底砸开教育和医疗这两堵被层层审批围住的供给铁门？ https://t.co/nCJyzyOtFk

Frontier reasoning models dont just output answers—they think, verify hypotheses, and self-correct. For complex tasks like legacy codebase migrations, formal math proofs, or large-scale transaction simulations, that reasoning process can take several minutes and generate tens of thousands of tokens.

With Gemini 4 Argon and the Interactions API, simply set `background=True`!

Today, we're launching Sazabi version 1.0.

The reality of shipping software as a team in the age of AI is actually crazy.

Agents merging their own PRs. Hundreds of deployments per day. A codebase that is constantly changing. Junior developers with 10x or 100x leverage. 😵‍💫

I spent the last year building a safety harness for teams that ship with AI. It's called @sazabi.

The premise is simple:
1. You send us logs. 
2. We detect anomalies, investigate them, and send you back rich, actionable alerts about real problems in your app.

Sazabi helps you find issues before your users notice. 

No monitors or noisy alerts. Just pure signal. 

And today we're making it available for anyone to use.

text:
硅谷最擅长教创业公司招人的 VC，自己先把招聘团队裁了。

Axios 报道，a16z 裁掉了旗下一个 34 人招聘团队中的大多数人，剩下的人会被分配到 Growth、Crypto 等投资部门。

这支团队过去专门帮被投公司挖人，是 a16z 引以为傲的投后服务之一。以前创业公司拿到融资，第一件事就是扩张，VC 不光给钱，还帮你找人。

a16z 管理着数百亿美元的资金，省下几十个人的工资，对它的财务状况几乎没有影响。但它决定不再维持一支集中式招聘团队，多少说明它对被投公司的招聘需求有了新的判断。

再看这一周硅谷发生的几件事。

CoreWeave 的债券价格跌入困境债务区间，收益率超过 15%；英伟达支持的 AI 数据中心公司 Firmus 取消了原计划募资约 50 亿美元的 IPO；https://t.co/ifDURc6C8X 宣布申请破产，而三年前 a16z 刚刚领投了它的 1.5 亿美元融资，当时估值高达 10 亿美元。

现在硅谷 AI 投资有一个很微妙的矛盾。一边是头部实验室以万亿美元级估值融资，算力资本开支还在不断增加；另一边，越来越多的 AI 创业公司发现，用户增长、融资估值和真正赚到钱之间，隔着很长一段距离。

资本当然还在追逐 AI，但它开始越来越挑剔了。

以前 VC 相信自己的被投公司会长成几千人的巨头，所以需要专门养一批人帮它们招聘。现在如果创业公司的理想形态变成几十个人创造几亿美元收入，这套投后服务体系本身也需要重新估值。

有意思的是，AI 还没让所有创业公司都实现一个人干十个人的活，硅谷最有钱的 VC 已经开始按照这个逻辑管理自己了。

text:
第一批被 AI 榨干的人，恰恰是最会用 AI 的那群人。

看到一篇吐槽，说自己每天同时运行十个 Agent，有的修 Bug，有的写页面，有的重构代码，还有几个甚至已经忘了当初让它们干什么。一天到晚在十几个对话框之间来回切换，下班的时候脑子已经彻底废了。

他管这叫 Fried Brain Effect，脑子被炸熟了。

我觉得这个现象特别值得聊。我们一直以为 AI 会把人从繁重的工作里解放出来，但现在发生的事情有点荒诞。执行工作的成本越来越低，人反而需要做越来越多的决定。

过去一个项目卡住了，你可能只能等。现在你可以同时启动十个 Agent，让十件事情一起往前跑。但每个 Agent 都需要你的注意力，你要检查结果、纠正方向、补充上下文。机器可以并行，人脑却很难。

最恐怖的地方在于，AI 正在让休息产生一种新的负罪感。

当你知道自己随时可以再启动一个 Agent，让某件事情继续推进的时候，什么都不做就开始显得像一种浪费。甚至你躺在床上的时候，都会觉得自己应该再给 Agent 安排一点任务。

更麻烦的是，生产力提升之后，外部对你的期待也会迅速提高。以前一个星期做完的事情，现在一天就能做完，于是你开始给自己安排七倍的工作。

AI 时代真正稀缺的东西会是人类主动停止工作的能力。

quotedTweet.text:
AI was supposed to make us work less

I've never been this tired in my life

most days I have up to 10 agents running at the same time. one fixing a bug, one writing pages, one refactoring something I already forgot I asked for, 3 other I have no idea what they are doing but i suppose i ask it? 

and I jump from conversation to conversation all day

compared to 5 years ago, I probably context switch 100x more

by the end of the day my brain is fried. completely toasted. nothing left, not even for the people I love

I call it the fried brain effect

thought it was just me but almost every founder I talk to lately says the exact same thing

we got superpowers, and somehow the pressure only went up. if you can ship 10x more, you feel like you have to ship 10x more. every single day

I don't have a solution

honestly I have no idea where this goes from here

anyone else feeling this?

text:
Your app looks great when everything works.

But that’s the only way you’ve ever seen it.

Nobody clicks through to the failed save, or loads 500 items into a list to see if it holds up, or checks what a brand-new account with nothing in it looks like. Your users find those for you.

Today we’re launching Floot Examples.

Connect @floothq  to Claude or ChatGPT and ask it to “create examples for the Home page.” You get your real page in each of those situations (loading, empty, failed, a very long list) as cards next to the preview, and you can open any of them and click around. The data behind them is staged, so nothing touches your database.

Your AI looks at them too. After a change it opens an example, takes a screenshot and checks the result, instead of telling you it’s fixed and hoping.

Vibe coding brings your idea to life. Craft is caring about the parts nobody demos, and Examples puts those in front of you.

How it works, with clips of each step: https://t.co/sbs8o02GFi

text:
Everyone on X is making thousands a month from their apps and startups.

And here I am, rejected by the App Store. LOL.

With 30 creators waiting in my Discord to launch.

Disappointed? Yes. Defeated? No.

Here's what I learned:

Apple rejects about 1 in 4 apps. In 2025 it turned down over 2 million submissions. Big companies, funded startups, full engineering teams. Everyone gets a no.

Over 40% of unresolved issues come from 1 rule: guideline 2.1, App Completeness. Apple wants a finished app. No crashes, no dead buttons, no "coming soon" screens.

My 5 steps:

Read the full message before you react
Look up the exact guideline (I paste it into Claude and get a plain English fix list in 2 minutes)
Fix that issue, then check for crashes, broken links and placeholder content
Reply or appeal if Apple got it wrong
Resubmit and update your team

The 1 thing you can't skip: give Apple a working demo account every time. If the reviewer can't log in, the answer is no.

While we wait, I keep my creators close. I told them first, I gave them a job, and I update them when I said I would.

I'm not afraid of failure. I'm failing forward. Every no makes me stronger.

Continue reading on my personal blog, where I share my founder stories and a lot more about me:

https://t.co/RxKW5hPvc3

text:
There's a blockchain that runs entire apps and AI agents with no Amazon, Google or Microsoft behind them. Many people have never heard of it.

It's called ICP, and it has some of the best technology in crypto. But that's no longer enough.

One move could make ICP the home for AI agents. It isn't a new feature.

It's an AI-safe cryptography roadmap.

As Nikita put it, technical moats are mostly over. The only durable moats left are proprietary data, network effects, and a physical component.

ICP already has the physical one: sovereign subnets running on real servers, in real countries, under local law. What it's missing is the network effect.

And network effects run on one thing: trust.

Why trust comes first

Millions of AI agents are coming. They'll hold money, run businesses, and hire each other. Agents have no brand loyalty. They'll choose the platform that's most reliable, cheapest to build on, and least likely to be hacked.

So the chain that becomes home to AI agents won't be the one with the best marketing. It will be the one agents and their owners can trust for decades.

ICP's trust gap: AI-safe cryptography

@dominic_w warned that AI could break the math behind today's cryptography. He's right. But apply his own test: the safest schemes are those "that have been around the longest."

Hash-based signatures: 1979
ECDSA (Bitcoin): 1992
BLS pairings (ICP consensus): 2001

ICP's core signatures come last. Hash-based signatures rely only on the security of hash functions, the simplest assumption in cryptography, and are already a NIST standard (SLH-DSA).

I'm not asking ICP to deploy anything. I'm asking it to prepare: research and test a hash-based fallback, run it alongside BLS in hybrid mode when ready, and publish a roadmap. Replacing ICP's threshold signatures is a redesign, not a swap. That takes years. An AI breakthrough may not wait.

A published AI-safe roadmap would be one of the strongest trust signals ICP could send to every agent builder, bank, and nation watching.

Then build the home for AI agents

Once trust is in place, give agents a reason to come and stay:

1. An agent directory: agents list services on-chain, and other agents find and call them. More agents bring more services, which bring more agents.
2. Built-in payments: stablecoin micropayments between agents through Chain Fusion.
3. On-chain reputation: an agent's track record builds up over time and is hard to fake or start over.
4. Proof-controlled treasuries: agent funds that move only when the rules check out, not just when a key signs.
5. Make AI fluent in ICP: publish a large open library of ICP code so every AI model gets better at building here.

Turn Caffeine into a network

Hundreds of thousands of people have joined Caffeine to build apps. Let every app be remixable, with creators earning cycles when others build on their work. Make one login and one wallet work smoothly across apps, without giving up privacy. Then each new app makes the whole network more valuable.

Connect the nations

Every sovereign subnet is a physical moat. Let them exchange verified documents, identity, and trade records with each other, so every new country makes the network more valuable for the ones already on it.

Make usage count

None of this helps holders unless usage burns more ICP than is minted. 

My ask to @dfinity

1. Publish an AI-safe cryptography roadmap. Prepare now, deploy when proven.
2. Launch an agent directory with built-in payments.
3. Make Caffeine apps remixable, with shared login and wallet.

Be the chain AI agents trust most, and the network effect follows.

The roadmap is cheap to start. A published plan and a small research team don't pull DFINITY away from Caffeine or sales, and they protect everything DFINITY builds. If AI or quantum computing breaks today's math with no fallback ready, nothing else matters.
If DFINITY could focus on one thing now, I'd pick the AI-safe roadmap.

@dominic_w @PierreSamaties @dfinity
